name: Apple M2 Max (38-core GPU, MacBook Pro 16-inch, Jan 2023)
memory_bandwidth_basis: Apple tech specs (support.apple.com/en-us/111340): M2 Max = 400 GB/s unified memory bandwidth across both GPU bins (30-core and 38-core). Unified pool, shared with CPU - not a dedicated VRAM bus.
notes:
M2 Max: 12-core CPU, 30- or 38-core GPU, 16-core Neural Engine, up to 96 GB unified memory, 400 GB/s. Included as the portable mid-tier between M1/M2 Ultra and M3/M4 Max. NOTE: unlike M3 Max (where the 14-core-CPU config drops to 300 GB/s), M2 Max holds 400 GB/s on both GPU bins per Apple's spec page - the config trap does not apply here.

UNIFIED MEMORY IS NOT VRAM: the GPU cannot address the whole pool; bandwidth is shared with CPU/Neural Engine; bigger capacity does not mean faster decode. See the standing caveat on apple-m3-max.

tdp_w null: Apple publishes no per-SoC power figure for the laptop.

MEMORY_BUS_WIDTH: null. Apple publishes memory BANDWIDTH only, never a bus width in bits for M-series parts; not back-computed (LPDDR5X pin rates vary by SKU). NO FIGURE WAS BACK-COMPUTED FROM BANDWIDTH.

Inference read: 400 GB/s shared unified bandwidth -> measured 8.8 tok/s on Llama-3.3-70B 4-bit (siliconscore row, see comm-apple-m2-max-llama33-70b-4bit-tg). 64 GB SKUs only fit a 70B Q4 at low context; the 96 GB top config is the capacity play.
